posts.author: Diode Holographer
posts.post_subject: A Couple More Questions About TEA
posts.content_md:
I'm excited about this idea and I've read plenty on it so far. I just have a couple questions that I haven't seen addressed.

Firstly, I notice that everyone who talks about it is using Plates as opposed to Film. Can this only be done with plates or is it just a pain to do it with film (do to it's flexibility) so people avoid it?

Also, I see several suggestions for drying, which seems to be a bit of an issue. I have not seen anyone say anything about "freeze drying". What if each time (through the whole process) I need to dry the film, I just throw it in a vacuum chamber and lower the pressure until the water evaporates off? Would the speed of the evaporation be too hard on the emulsion or what do you think about that?

Does this technique work for white light viewable transmission holograms? This may seem like a stupid question, but I've never seen a white light viewable TH so I don't know exactly what they look like.

Thanks in advance.

posts.topic_title: A Couple More Questions About TEA
posts.author: Ed Wesly
posts.post_subject: A Couple More Questions About TEA
posts.content_md:
From above:

> I've never seen a white light viewable TH so I don't know exactly what they look like.

I should sure hope that you have seen one, if you have ever looked at a credit card holo or magazine cover, etc. The embossed holos are white light transmission images, metalized so that they don't have to be back lit. But their fringe structure is of the white light transmission variety, as opposed to the true reflection style.

> Does this technique work for white light viewable transmission holograms?

Color in the WLT holo is controlled by geometry: where the slit-like H1 is with respect to the H2 copy plate. What would happen if you TEA-treated a WLT holo is that the replay reference angle would be quite different than the recording reference beam angle. If you ask in which direction, I would reply, as they say in the math books, that this is an exercise for the student!

posts.content_md: Another method to manipulate the colors of images in transmission holograms is to make it an "achromatic", or "open aperture" transfer and emboss it on colored plastic. Or use a selective mirror. Or a reflection hologram behind it.

posts.content_md:
Ironic this should get brought back up, I've been playing with TEA for the past few days now.

I gotta say I like it. I'm having some minor trouble getting some colors and I think it might be my squeegying (sp?) that needs work. Either tonight or tomorow I'm going to try letting them air dry. 

I used a fairly cheap TEA from here [http://www.chemistrystore.com/search.cg ... arch2.y=12](http://www.chemistrystore.com/search.cgi?keywords=triethanolamine&Click+to+Search2.x=8&Click+to+Search2.y=12) and I have not experienced this milky film that I've seen so many complain about.

I understand that not every question I ask will be answerable, but the reason I ask them is because I want to rely on "trial and error" as little as possible.
